title: Chief Engineer Operations H/F
description: 📍 Paris / Île-de-France | Environnement Data Center | CDI | Périmètre multisite Rejoignez mon client au cœur des infrastructures critiques. Au sein d'un nouvel pôle d'expertise technique transverse , vous devenez le référent technique des opérations sur plusieurs sites stratégiques en France, avec un périmètre prioritaire couvrant notamment deux sites. Ce poste s'adresse à un profil expérimenté qui souhaite aller au-delà de l'expertise technique pure et jouer un rôle central dans la structuration des opérations d'un acteur Data Center en pleine croissance . Vos missions Votre rôle Le Chief Engineer intervient comme référent technique et opérationnel multisite . Vous êtes à la fois : un expert technique capable de challenger les équipes et les prestataires ; un référent opérationnel garant de la sécurisation des opérations ; un acteur transverse capable de fédérer des équipes aux profils et niveaux d'expérience différents. title: Technicien Réseaux & Télécom Itinérant (H/F)
description: Poste : Technicien (position 2.1, coefficient 275, convention collective Syntec) · Basé en France · Interventions sur notre infrastructure, partout en France et à l'international Vous aimez le terrain, les sites qui ne se ressemblent pas et le moment où le lien monte enfin. Chez Azurreo, vous installez, raccordez, testez et dépannez notre propre infrastructure réseaux et télécoms, celle qui fait tourner nos activités et nos plateformes à travers le monde. Un poste de terrain, mais avec des horaires fixes du lundi au vendredi, des heures supplémentaires payées et inscrites au contrat, des frais avancés par l'entreprise, et vos habilitations financées si vous ne les avez pas encore. Qui nous sommes Azurreo est la branche télécommunications et technologies de Seelon Holdings, groupe d'investissement international présent sur quatre continents. Nous sommes un acteur de référence du test de performance des réseaux : notre plateforme SignalVerify mesure la qualité de service et la qualité d'expérience des réseaux dans plus de 144 pays. Depuis plus de quinze ans, nous accompagnons opérateurs télécoms, intégrateurs, constructeurs et grandes entreprises dans le déploiement et la maintenance de leurs infrastructures en Europe, au Moyen-Orient et en Afrique : plus de 250 projets livrés dans plus de 25 pays. Pour soutenir cette activité, Azurreo exploite et entretient son propre réseau d'infrastructures techniques en France et à l'international. C'est cette infrastructure que vous aurez en charge : celle qui permet à nos équipes et à nos plateformes de fonctionner, jour après jour, partout où nous sommes présents. À quoi ressemble une semaine Aucune semaine n'est identique : Installation. Montage d'une baie sur l'un de nos sites, raccordement, brassage, étiquetage, tests, mise en service. Dépannage. Une liaison qui ne monte pas depuis trois jours. Le plan de câblage ne correspond pas à l'existant. Vous cherchez, vous mesurez, vous trouvez, et vous écrivez ce que vous avez trouvé. Datacenter. Rack & stack, cross-connects, mise en place d'équipements actifs. Déploiement multi-sites. Plusieurs de nos sites dans la même semaine : bornes Wi-Fi, switches, configuration de base, comptes rendus. Missions à l'international. Certaines semaines vous emmènent sur nos sites hors de France. Journées base arrière. Préparation du matériel, gestion des stocks et de l'outillage, maintenance préventive, mise à jour des tickets. Toutes les semaines ne sont pas des semaines de route. Ce que vous ferez Installation et déploiement. Installation et mise en service d'équipements télécoms et informatiques sur nos sites. Câblage, raccordement et brassage. Déploiement de routeurs, switches, bornes Wi-Fi et équipements de connectivité. Préparation du matériel avant intervention, participation aux migrations et déploiements sur nos infrastructures. Maintenance et support technique. Maintenance préventive et corrective de nos équipements. Diagnostic des incidents et mise en œuvre des dépannages. Remplacement et reconfiguration d'équipements défectueux. Vérification du bon fonctionnement après intervention. Suivi et reporting. Rédaction des comptes rendus d'intervention, mise à jour des outils de suivi et des tickets d'incidents, gestion du matériel confié, participation aux stocks et inventaires, remontée des anomalies aux équipes concernées. Qualité et sécurité. Respect des procédures qualité et sécurité d'Azurreo et des consignes propres à chaque site, usage approprié des équipements et outils mis à disposition. Les technologies que vous rencontrerez Réseaux : TCP/IP, VLAN, DHCP, DNS, VPN, LAN / WAN Constructeurs : Cisco, Huawei, Aruba, Fortinet, Juniper Télécoms : fibre optique, FTTH, FTTO, RJ45, brassage, baies informatiques Datacenter : rack & stack, cross-connect, installation, maintenance Vous ne maîtrisez pas tout cela ? Personne ne le maîtrise entièrement. Nous cherchons de bonnes bases techniques, de la curiosité et de la rigueur. Le reste s'apprend. Parlons des déplacements franchement Les déplacements en France et à l'international font partie intégrante du poste : ce n'est pas occasionnel, c'est une exigence. Le rythme varie réellement selon les projets : certaines semaines sans déplacement, d'autres avec des découchés en France ou à l'étranger. Nous ne garantissons pas de rythme fixe. Le véhicule utilitaire est mis à disposition pour les interventions en France : ce n'est pas un véhicule de fonction et il ne rentre pas chez vous le soir. Les imprévus font partie du métier : matériel non livré, local fermé, câblage existant non conforme au plan. Il y a de la manutention, des faux plafonds et des locaux techniques exigus. En contrepartie : tous les frais professionnels sont pris en charge en amont, les horaires restent fixes, les heures supplémentaires sont payées, et vous ne passez pas vos journées au même bureau à faire la même chose. Le profil que nous cherchons Indispensable Résider en France Permis B en cours de validité Disponible pour des déplacements fréquents, en France et à l'international Formation ou expérience dans les télécommunications, les réseaux ou les infrastructures techniques Connaissances en réseaux informatiques, câblage RJ45 et fibre optique Capacité à diagnostiquer et résoudre des incidents techniques Français courant, anglais niveau A2 minimum (à l'oral et pour lire de la documentation technique) Maîtrise des outils bureautiques courants Autonomie, rigueur, organisation Capacité à travailler en mobilité et à vous adapter à des environnements techniques variés Apprécié, mais pas exigé Anglais au-delà du niveau A2 Expérience sur équipements Cisco, Huawei, Aruba, Fortinet ou Juniper Fibre optique : raccordement, soudure, mesures. Wi-Fi, datacenter Certifications réseau (CCNA ou équivalent) et habilitations à jour : AIPR, habilitation électrique, travail en hauteur, CACES nacelle, SST. Si vous ne les avez pas, nous organisons la formation pour que vous les obteniez. Formation : Bac Pro SN, BTS SIO, BTS CIEL, BTS Télécommunications, BUT/DUT Réseaux & Télécommunications, Licence professionnelle Réseaux, ou expérience équivalente. Ce que vous avez fait compte autant que ce que vous avez étudié. Ce que nous vous offrons Des horaires fixes du lundi au vendredi et pas d'astreinte Des heures supplémentaires payées, majorées et inscrites au contrat Des frais avancés par l'entreprise Vos certifications et habilitations financées si vous ne les avez pas Une formation continue réelle, avec accès direct aux ingénieurs de l'entreprise Des missions variées, en France et à l'international, sur notre propre infrastructure Une entreprise internationale à taille humaine Le processus de recrutement Étude de votre candidature par notre équipe recrutement Entretien RH, en visio (30 à 40 min), avec le recrutement, sur votre parcours, vos attentes et le poste en détail Entretien technique (45 à 60 min) avec votre futur manager, sur la technique, le terrain et votre méthode Entretien final (30 min) avec Adam Anbari, gérant d'Azurreo EURL L'embauche est conditionnée à une visite médicale d'aptitude au poste. Comment candidater Envoyez-nous votre CV. Pas besoin de lettre de motivation ; quelques lignes sur une intervention dont vous êtes fier (ce qu'il y avait à faire, ce qui a coincé, comment vous l'avez réglé) nous parlent davantage. Azurreo étudie toutes les candidatures à compétences égales, sans distinction d'origine, de sexe, d'âge, de situation personnelle ou de handicap. title: Performance Marketing Manager
description: Why we do what we do The mind is our window to the world. It can paint everything outside in grey or in bright colors. Whoever finds access to that window can change their perspective every day, and psychological hurdles can become chances to grow. Happiness spreads from one person to the next and across a whole society, like a quiet revolution, one mind at a time. Who we are Our mission inspires us and challenges us. Our skills, thoughts and ideas go into a product that reaches thousands of people, and that brings responsibility with it. The work asks for passion, integrity and the courage to try things no one has tried before. A team full of people who are crazy enough to think they can change the world they live in. Yes, we are a hardworking team, but not for us alone, not for money or personal fame, but for the people we serve at the center of our efforts: Our team, clients, psychologists on our platform and supporters across the country. Why this role exists Aepsy serves three audiences, each with its own timeline. Clients need support now. Psychologists are building their practice. Employers are deciding whether to unlock access for their whole team. This role leads performance marketing for all three: how people find Aepsy, what actually works, and what the numbers suggest we do next. Marketing at Aepsy is a small, focused team, and every role has a clear place in it. The Creative Marketing Lead owns copy and shapes the campaigns. The Art Director builds the visual language. The Growth Performance Architect owns the measurement architecture. You work closely with all three, bringing campaigns to the right people through the right channels, finding out what worked, and helping the team decide what to keep, change or stop. Performance with principles Our values shape how we advertise. Privacy is non-negotiable. Anyone visiting a mental health platform deserves the highest level of privacy and data security. That means no urgency or fear in our messages, no before-and-after claims, and no targeting or retargeting based on health data or other sensitive personal information. Sometimes this makes a number harder to reach. It also builds trust that lasts, and that trust is why people choose Aepsy. If strong performance combined with strong principles sounds like the challenge you’ve been looking for, we’d love to hear from you. What you’ll do Own performance across all funnels. Clients may decide within days. Employers take longer and involve several people. Together with the colleagues closest to each audience, you define what success means for each one. Run paid media end to end on Meta, Google, TikTok and LinkedIn. That covers structure, bidding, audiences, creative rotation, and both awareness and conversion, plus the judgement to know which of the two you’re working on. Read the numbers and get more out of them. The Growth Performance Architect builds the measurement setup with you. You turn it into insights the team can act on. Turn patterns into decisions. Why do people who considered Aepsy drop off before deciding? Does the response to a creative suggest it should run weekly rather than monthly? Answering questions like these is the core of the role. Shape how people find support. Search is changing fast, and new ways of discovering things are emerging. You’ll help decide how people find Aepsy when they need it most. Help build the team’s marketing rhythm. You’ll set up the flow for campaigns, newsletters and more, from first idea to delivery, so the whole team can rely on it. title: Flight Test Instrumentation & Data Engineer
description: The Flight Test Instrumentation (FTI) & Data Engineer will be responsible for the end-to-end handling, quality assurance, accessibility, and long-term management of all flight data. The primary objective is to ensure that full-aircraft data, from the onboard sensors and DAQ systems to the final processing tools, is available to every engineering team through a reliable, efficient, and standardized workflow. Tasks Flight Test Instrumentation (FTI) & DAQ Pipeline Manage the data pipeline from the physical sensor and Data Acquisition (DAQ) level for the full aircraft, ensuring seamless and accurate transmission into the telemetry and storage systems. Maintain sensor configuration, calibration records, and metadata to guarantee the accurate translation of raw physical signals into usable engineering units. Collaborate with hardware, software and integration teams to define sensor requirements, DAQ architectures, scaling, and telemetry bandwidth allocations. Troubleshoot and resolve data anomalies at the DAQ and sensor level (e.g., signal noise, dropouts, faulty scaling) before they propagate into downstream databases. Data Infrastructure & Accessibility Maintain reliable extraction of flight data from InfluxDB. Develop and maintain standardized local data structures for analysis, plotting, and visualization. Optimize access to large flight datasets while minimizing CPU and memory usage. Design and maintain an efficient local storage solution for processed flight data. Support future improvements to the flight data architecture as storage requirements, sensor counts, and analysis needs continue to evolve. Data Quality & Analysis Support Maintain derived datasets to ensure common calculations and signals are shared consistently across teams. Ensure strict timing synchronization and timestamp accuracy across all recorded data, from the sensor acquisition point to the database. Monitor data quality, completeness, and integrity throughout the entire pipeline. Provide fast data previews for rapid post-flight reviews. Enable efficient access to high-frequency sensor data for detailed engineering investigations. Support custom querying of processed datasets. Requirements Education & Experience Bachelor’s or Master’s degree in Aerospace Engineering, Computer Science, Data Engineering, or a related technical field. 3+ years of professional experience in test instrumentation, data acquisition (DAQ), or sensor-to-database time-series data engineering (aerospace, automotive, or racing/motorsports preferred). Hands-on experience working directly with physical aircraft/vehicle sensor installations, DAQ hardware, and telemetry pipelines. Technical & Domain Expertise 1. Hardware, Sensors & DAQ Architecture Strong understanding of physical sensors (e.g., strain gauges, accelerometers, thermocouples, pressure transducers, RTDs, LVDTs, pitot-static tubes). Demonstrated knowledge of signal conditioning, sampling rate selection, anti-aliasing filtering, scaling, and sensor calibration procedures. 2. Data Infrastructure & Software Development Proficient in Python or MATLAB for data analysis, automated data processing, and visualization library development (e.g., Pandas, NumPy, SciPy). Experience working with time-series databases, specifically InfluxDB (or similar engines), including writing efficient queries (Flux/InfluxQL) and data retrieval pipelines. Solid foundation in data structures and memory/CPU optimization when handling high-memory high-frequency continuous time-series datasets. 3. Data Integrity & Signal Processing Experience with timestamping and clock synchronization protocols across distributed DAQ hardware and storage nodes. Knowledge of basic digital signal processing (DSP) concepts (filtering, FFT, spectral analysis, decimation/resampling). Soft Skills & Work Style Cross-functional communication: Ability to bridge the gap between hardware technicians, flight physics/aerodynamics engineers, and software teams. Detail-oriented mindset: Uncompromising rigor regarding calibration metadata, unit conversions, and data accuracy. Adaptability: Drive to continuously improve data infrastructure as aircraft sensor counts, test frequencies, and analytical needs expand. Preferred / Bonus Qualifications Knowledge of standard FAA / EASA flight test instrumentation requirements or military flight test standards (e.g. IRIG 106). Familiarity with dashboarding tools (e.g., Grafana) for rapid post-flight previews and real-time telemetry display. Experience with version control systems (Git) and CI/CD pipelines for internal engineering tool distribution. Direct experience with DAQ systems and digital bus protocols (CAN bus, ARINC 429, MIL-STD-1553, Ethernet/UDP, PCM). Familiarity with binary flight data formats (e.g., IRIG 106 Chapter 10/11, MDF/MF4, HDF5, Parquet, or custom binary loggers). Experience with performing on-aircraft hardware troubleshooting (e.g., tracking down ground loops, signal noise, dropouts, or faulty scaling). title: Founding lead Product Designer
description: Raison is on a mission to provide humans with better skills so they can feel confident and have more opportunities in the AI era. We help companies make sure 100% their teams master AI, directly in the flow of work (Teams, Slack) so that AI knowledge spreads across the organization instead of pooling in a handful of champions. We are passionate entrepreneurs believing that the ongoing AI revolution should be shared by all employees; and that the future of corporate interactions should not be restricted to private human-machine chats. Raison is capturing what champions create with AI, turning it into shared, governed skills, and propagating them so everyone feels capable and empowered; acting as a powerful lever to accelerate the AI transformation of corporates. We recently raised €2m from a top French VC + BPI and a selection of high-profile business angels who believe AI mastery is the highest-leverage application of AI inside companies. Tasks User Research & Discovery Own field research: contextual inquiry, user interviews, and observation of how teams actually work with AI and where it breaks. Build and maintain a deep understanding of our core users — individual contributors, champions, managers, and corporate buyers — and the context they operate in. Synthesize messy field data into sharp, actionable insight: jobs-to-be-done, adoption blockers, and the conditions under which a skill transfers between people. Establish a continuous discovery habit so research is a foundational reflex, and champion the user's perspective in every product decision. Product & Experience Design What our experts do by hand today is the spec for what the product must automate tomorrow. Your job is to watch that closely enough to design it. Design the surfaces: the client dashboard execs present to their board, the internal console our experts use to run a dozen live communities at once, and the conversations themselves. Most of our product lives inside someone else's client. You are designing in Teams and Slack, not screens we control — no onboarding, no landing page, no second chance. A four-minute message to an accountant who has never opened Copilot is the hardest design problem we have. Work mostly on enterprise, and partly on higher education, where we also have live deployments. Two audiences, two vocabularies, one product: part of your job is deciding what stays shared and what has to differ, so we build one coherent system rather than two half-products. Work hand-in-hand with our AI product engineers so your field learnings ship as features, then get re-tested at the next pilot. Own the design system: components, tokens, patterns, and the copy that goes with them. Requirements 4–8 years in product design, UX design, or a hybrid design-research role, ideally on complex, multi-user B2B products. A strong portfolio that shows both craft and thinking: we want to see how you operated, not just what shipped. A skilled researcher who can design a study, run it in the wild, and turn qualitative chaos into clear direction. Experience designing inside environments you don't control - a messaging client, an extension, an embedded product - or a clear appetite for it. Comfortable designing for AI-driven and adaptive experiences, where the interface has to handle uncertainty, personalization, and non-linear workflows. Excellent visual and interaction design skills: typography, spacing, motion, and the small details that build trust. Autonomous and opinionated, but you hold your opinions loosely when the evidence says otherwise. Genuine curiosity about AI and how people actually learn at work. Fluent in French and English, spoken and written. Spanish is a plus. You want the ownership, equity, and career-defining challenge that only comes from being early. Bonus: deeply passionate about something outside of work. Benefits A founding role with equity and direct influence on company strategy. Competitive salary, benchmarked to the Paris startup ecosystem. Flexibility: remote-friendly with regular in-person collaboration in Paris and an office in Montmartre with a beautiful Sacré-Coeur view. A front-row seat to one of the most important shifts in how humans learn. A small, sharp team that ships fast and trusts each other to figure things out. If you care deeply about making powerful tools feel human and want to shape a product from the very beginning, this is your role. Apply now and help us build the future of learning. Raison is an equal opportunity employer. We welcome applicants of all backgrounds and are committed to building a diverse, inclusive team. Find Jobs in France on Arbeitnow

title: Responsable Accompagnement Clients - Transition énergétique des bâtiments
description: Chez Lowit, nous avons une ambition : accélérer et massifier la transition énergétique des bâtiments tertiaires. Face à la hausse des coûts de l'énergie, aux enjeux climatiques et aux évolutions réglementaires, les gestionnaires de patrimoine ont besoin d'outils fiables, mais aussi d'un accompagnement de qualité pour passer à l'action. C'est pourquoi nous avons développé une plateforme SaaS qui permet de créer le jumeau numérique des bâtiments, de piloter les consommations énergétiques et de construire des trajectoires d'investissement réalistes, chiffrées et adaptées aux enjeux de chaque organisation. Aujourd'hui, nous accompagnons plusieurs centaines de collectivités et d'entreprises partout en France dans leurs projets de transition énergétique. PME lyonnaise en forte croissance, nous recherchons des collaborateurs qui souhaitent avoir un impact concret, prendre des responsabilités et contribuer à une aventure collective porteuse de sens. Vos missions Chez Lowit, nous accompagnons chaque jour des collectivités, des entreprises et des établissements publics dans la gestion et la transition énergétique de leur patrimoine immobilier. Notre plateforme leur permet de mieux connaître leurs bâtiments, de piloter leurs consommations, d'anticiper les obligations réglementaires et de construire des trajectoires d'investissement cohérentes. Parce qu'une plateforme ne crée de valeur que lorsqu'elle est pleinement appropriée par ses utilisateurs, nous accordons une place essentielle à l'accompagnement de nos clients. C'est précisément la mission de notre équipe Accompagnement Clients. Pour accompagner notre croissance, nous recherchons aujourd'hui un(e) Responsable Accompagnement Clients . Vous deviendrez l'interlocuteur privilégié d'un portefeuille de collectivités, d'entreprises et d'établissements publics. Votre mission sera de construire une relation de confiance durable avec vos clients, de comprendre leurs enjeux et de les accompagner dans l'utilisation de nos solutions afin qu'ils en tirent le meilleur parti. Concrètement, vous serez amené à : Accompagner vos clients tout au long de leur parcours chez Lowit au travers d'échanges réguliers (téléphone, visioconférences, réunions et e-mails). Développer une compréhension approfondie de leurs enjeux afin de leur apporter un accompagnement pertinent et personnalisé. Les conseiller sur les sujets liés à la transition énergétique des bâtiments : réglementation, stratégie patrimoniale, performance énergétique, dispositifs d'aides, mécanismes de financement... en vous appuyant sur les experts internes lorsque cela est nécessaire. Réaliser ponctuellement des missions de conseil directement chez les clients afin de fiabiliser leur patrimoine, mettre à jour leurs données, construire des scénarios personnalisés et restituer des plans d'action auprès de leurs équipes de direction ou de leurs élus. Identifier les besoins émergents, détecter les opportunités d'accompagnement complémentaires et remonter les signaux business aux équipes concernées. Animer des webinaires, partager les bonnes pratiques et contribuer au développement de la communauté d'utilisateurs Lowit. Faire remonter les retours clients et les besoins fonctionnels afin de contribuer à l'amélioration continue de notre plateforme et de nos services. Vous travaillerez en étroite collaboration avec les équipes Projets, Produit, Commerce et nos experts techniques afin de garantir un accompagnement de grande qualité. Ce poste est avant tout un métier de relation client, de conseil et d'accompagnement . Vous ne serez pas seul face aux problématiques techniques : vous pourrez vous appuyer sur les expertises présentes chez Lowit. En revanche, votre capacité à écouter, comprendre les enjeux de vos clients et construire avec eux une relation de confiance sera déterminante dans leur réussite… et dans la nôtre. Vos compétences Nous recherchons avant tout une personne qui aime construire des relations de confiance dans la durée. Ingénieur(e) de formation ou diplômé(e) d'un Bac+5 dans les domaines de l'énergie, du bâtiment, de la thermique ou de l'immobilier, vous souhaitez mettre votre expertise au service de l'accompagnement client. Vous aimez comprendre les problématiques de vos interlocuteurs, les accompagner dans leurs projets et leur apporter des conseils concrets. Curieux(se), à l'écoute et pédagogue, vous appréciez autant les échanges humains que les sujets techniques. Une première expérience dans le conseil, la gestion de projet, le Customer Success ou l'accompagnement client constitue un véritable atout. Au-delà de votre parcours, nous serons particulièrement attentifs à votre capacité à : Créer une relation de confiance avec vos clients et communiquer avec aisance, aussi bien à l'oral qu'à l'écrit. Comprendre les enjeux techniques, réglementaires et patrimoniaux liés à la transition énergétique des bâtiments, ou avoir l'envie de développer rapidement cette expertise. Faire preuve de curiosité et d'une réelle envie d'apprendre dans un secteur en constante évolution. Organiser votre activité et prioriser efficacement les sollicitations d'un portefeuille clients. Travailler en équipe et mobiliser les bonnes expertises internes lorsque la situation l'exige. Être à l'aise avec les outils numériques et les environnements SaaS. Une connaissance des secteurs de l'énergie, du bâtiment, de l'immobilier ou des collectivités territoriales sera appréciée. Enfin, si vous aimez décrocher votre téléphone pour échanger avec vos clients, créer une relation durable et les accompagner bien au-delà de la simple utilisation d'un logiciel, vous vous sentirez probablement à votre place chez Lowit. title: Clinical Data Manager 50%
description: Join HEMEX, A European Contract Research Organization based in Liestal, Switzerland, dedicated to advancing global healthcare through innovative biotechnology research. As a Medical Monitor specializing in Pharmacovigilance and Medical Device Safety, you'll play a crucial role in ensuring the safety and efficacy of groundbreaking pharmaceutical, biotech, and medtech solutions. With our comprehensive clinical development services, including regulatory support and quality assurance, you'll have the opportunity to work on multinational clinical trials and contribute to the translation of novel concepts into market-ready solutions. Tasks The Clinical Data Manager is responsible for the planning, setup, conduct, cleaning, reconciliation, and closeout of clinical trial databases. The role ensures that clinical trial data are complete, consistent, accurate, traceable, and ready for statistical analysis and database lock. The Clinical Data Manager works closely with Clinical Operations, CRAs, Medical Monitors, Pharmacovigilance, Biostatistics, investigators, and sponsors throughout the study lifecycle. Functional Responsabilities: 1. Study Setup and Database Build Translate clinical trial protocols and endpoints into electronic Case Report Forms (eCRFs). Develop eCRF specifications in alignment with applicable CDISC (CDASH and SDTM) standards where required. Develop and maintain the Data Management Plan (DMP), the Data Validation Plan, and the eCRF Completion Guidelines. Define data handling, data transfer, reconciliation, and data security processes in compliance with applicable data protection requirements (e.g., GDPR and the Swiss FADP). Develop Edit Check Specifications and automated validation rules. Support database configuration and testing. Lead or coordinate User Acceptance Testing (UAT) of the Electronic Data Capture (EDC) system. Ensure database readiness and documented approval prior to study go-live. Train investigators and site staff on eCRF completion and EDC use, and support kick-off and investigator meetings as required. 2. Study Conduct and Data Cleaning Monitor incoming clinical trial data for completeness, consistency, and quality. Review data listings and identify missing, inconsistent, or implausible data. Generate, review, and track data queries to clinical trial sites. Use R programming to support data cleaning, validation, and preparation of clean datasets for Biostatistics, preferably following SDTM standards (ADaM derivations remain with Biostatistics), with appropriate documentation and quality control. Monitor query resolution and ensure that outstanding discrepancies are appropriately addressed. Maintain accurate documentation of data cleaning activities. Prepare data management status and metrics reports (e.g., query rates, data-entry timelines) for the project team and sponsors, and support risk-based quality management. 3. External Data Reconciliation Coordinate integration and reconciliation of external data sources with the clinical database. Define and agree data transfer agreements and specifications with external data vendors. Reconcile central laboratory data, ePRO/eCOA data, IRT data, imaging data, and other external datasets where applicable. Ensure that data transfers are complete, accurate, documented, and appropriately version-controlled. 4. Medical Coding Coordinate or perform medical coding of: Adverse events using MedDRA. Medical history using MedDRA. Concomitant medications using WHODrug or applicable standards. Ensure coding is consistent and appropriately reviewed, and that dictionary versions are documented and upgrades are managed in a controlled manner. Resolve coding discrepancies according to predefined procedures. 5. SAE and Safety Data Reconciliation Reconcile serious adverse events between the clinical database (EDC) and the pharmacovigilance/safety database at agreed intervals and prior to interim analyses and database lock. Work closely with Medical Monitors and Pharmacovigilance personnel to investigate discrepancies. Ensure that safety data are complete and consistent across relevant systems. 6. Database Lock and Study Closeout Coordinate the Lock Readiness Review. Confirm that critical data fields are complete. Ensure outstanding queries are closed or appropriately justified. Ensure protocol deviations and relevant data issues are appropriately documented. Coordinate final clean-file review with CRAs, Medical Monitors, Biostatisticians, and other relevant stakeholders. Execute or coordinate database lock according to approved procedures. Prepare data cuts and transfers for interim analyses and DSMB/DMC reviews as required. Ensure appropriate documentation of database lock activities. Support archiving and audit readiness, including metadata and audit trail documentation, and filing of data management documents in the Trial Master File (TMF). Keep documentation and handover notes up to date so that the named backup can cover planned and unplanned absences. Requirements Bachelor's or Master's degree in Life Sciences, Clinical Data Management, Pharmacy, Biostatistics, Computer Science, or a related discipline. At least 2 years of experience in clinical data management within a CRO, pharmaceutical, biotechnology, or medical device environment. Experience with EDC systems and clinical trial databases. Knowledge of clinical data management processes and database lifecycle management. Experience with eCRF development, edit checks, data cleaning, query management, and database lock. Knowledge of MedDRA and WHODrug preferred. Knowledge of CDISC (CDASH and SDTM) standards preferred. Knowledge of ICH-GCP and clinical research regulations (including requirements for computerized systems and electronic records, and data protection). Experience with R for data cleaning, validation, and listings; Python is an advantage. Strong attention to detail and data quality mindset. Structured and process-oriented working style. Strong organizational and project coordination skills. Ability to identify and resolve data discrepancies. Strong communication skills. Fluent English (written and spoken). Ability to work effectively across Clinical Operations, Pharmacovigilance, Medical Monitoring, and Biostatistics. Strong commitment to SOP compliance and continuous improvement. Ability to manage multiple studies and competing priorities. Benefits Flexible working arrangements and hybrid work options Modern, international and entrepreneurial working environment Opportunities for professional growth and continuous learning High level of autonomy and responsibility Collaborative team culture with direct communication and short decision-making paths Central location with good public transport connections Opportunity to work with innovative companies and projects in a dynamic industry Join HEMEX AG as a Clinical Data Manager (50%) to drive innovation in global healthcare. Collaborate on multinational trials with a leading European CRO in a dynamic, supportive environment. Find more English Speaking Jobs in Switzerland on Arbeitnow

title: Engineering Delivery & Operations Manager
description: Joining Weezevent means working on tangible solutions used at international festivals (Hellfest, Boomtown, Tomorrowland, Lollapalooza, Boom), major sporting events (Formula 1, the Olympic Games, Euro fan zones), and high-volume live experiences. Weezevent builds the technology behind live events: ticketing , cashless payment , CRM , staff solutions and access control . We are about 100 people in the tech team (engineering and product organisation), part of a group that has grown both organically and through acquisitions, so our teams span several countries and cultures. We are at an inflection point. We are opening a focused 12–18 month window to invest heavily in the foundations of our main product, WeezTicket: paying down technical debt, tightening our architecture, and setting ourselves up for the next phase of growth. To run that program, we’re hiring an Engineering Delivery & Operations Manager (M/F, based in Clichy) to own its delivery. Vos missions This is a two-part role, and the first part is where you’ll spend most of your first year. Part one : deliver the program . A board of our most experienced engineers is defining the architectural direction and producing a large backlog of clean-up and improvement work. That work will be delivered by several external squads brought in for the program. You own the delivery layer between them: getting squads stood up and productive on time, tracking each one’s pace and quality, and keeping the whole program on schedule. Stand up and onboard external squads, around 20 developers across 5 to 6 squads, on time : access, environments, documentation, and a well-scoped first backlog ready before they start Track the delivery pace of each squad against its commitments, and keep a clear program-level view of what’s on track, slipping, or blocked Hold squads to the quality bar set by the architectural board : tests, reviews, and no new debt introduced while removing old debt Manage cross-squad dependencies so work lands in the right order Track program spend against budget and manage the relationships with the partners supplying the squads Report program status to the CTO and the board on a regular cadence Part two : become the operational backbone of engineering. As the program matures, you’ll take on the people-operations side of the organisation: helping our managers run great 1:1s and reviews, coordinating the performance cycle, keeping an eye on team capacity and wellbeing, and bringing rigour to tooling and budget. This is what makes the role a long-term home rather than a temporary program job. You’ll work closely with the CTO, the architectural board, our 4 Team Leads, and the external partners supplying the squads. You won’t set the technical strategy or write the code, you’ll make sure the right work gets delivered, on time, at the right quality. Help 4 Team Leads and 6 Squad Leads run consistent 1:1s and grow as managers Coordinate the performance review cycle and make sure follow-up actions actually happen Keep visibility on team capacity, absences, and early signals of overload or burnout Bring structure to tech budget tracking and to the governance of our tools and licences Support hiring and internal mobility alongside our recruitment team Vos compétences Must-haves Experience running a multi-squad delivery program end to end: ideally involving external agencies, consultancies, or contract teams A track record of onboarding external teams onto an existing codebase and getting them productive quickly Comfort owning a backlog, a schedule, and a budget across several parallel workstreams at once The ability to track pace and quality per team and raise problems early, with data Genuine tech literacy: you understand what developers do, can navigate a Jira board, and know what technical debt actually means Fluent French and English What makes you a strong long-term fit Some experience coaching or supporting managers, or running a performance cycle in a tech company A background that touched engineering, delivery, project management, or product before moving toward operations Analytical rigour: you’re comfortable with numbers, dashboards, and cost reports Direct, honest communication and real discretion with sensitive information Nice to have A third language (German or Dutch is a real plus given our footprint) Experience working across France, the UK, the Netherlands, or Germany, and an understanding of how management styles differ across them This is not A role that sets architecture or writes code; that’s the board and the squads A pure recruiter or a corporate-HR profile with no delivery or engineering exposure A process-for-process’s-sake job. We want impact, not bureaucracy The recruitment process HR interview - background and soft skills Interview with CTO - technical discussion All our positions are open to people with disabilities. Why it's a good move You’ll run a high-visibility program with the direct backing of the CTO and the most senior engineers in the company, in an organisation that has decided to genuinely invest in its technical foundations rather than just talk about it. And when the program lands, you’ll have built yourself a permanent, central role at the heart of how our engineering organisation runs. Find Jobs in France on Arbeitnow

title: Product Frontend Engineer
description: quinn is becoming the way people employ, across the globe, through one app. quinn is an app-based, managed payroll and employment-administration service. We run it for private households employing a cleaner, nanny, or caretaker, and for businesses that manage employment relationships at scale. The customer stays the legal employer: quinn registers the employment, runs payroll, and handles social insurance, taxes, and filings on their behalf, automated end to end. Where everyone else sells software, quinn sells the outcome. We don't sell payroll software. We run payroll. The purpose behind it is simple: Fair employment. For all. Correct and fair employment, made simple and accessible for any employer and any employee, in any market quinn enters. Where this is going Think about what Revolut did to banking. All of the complexity (the regulation, the clearing, the compliance) handled invisibly in the background, and one simple experience at the front. Nobody using Revolut thinks about what happens behind the screen when they open a new account, swap currencies or send money abroad. It just works, in a couple of taps. Nobody should have to think about it in order to employ someone either. That is what quinn is building, and it is further along than most people assume: a profitable core business, running today in Switzerland, Germany and the UK, expanding into new markets both by launching and by acquiring. By 2030 quinn intends to be the destination brand for fair employment across six countries and more, on one platform, with one experience. One platform means one frontend. One experience means it looks and behaves like quinn whether you are in Zurich or in London, a household or a company. In this strategy that is not a nice-to-have. It is the strategy. Which is why the surface matters more than anything else. Everything quinn does is designed to disappear. The interface is the only part the customer ever sees, and it is the whole proof that the complexity behind it is really handled. Why this role exists Today , quinn runs on several separate web apps: one per product and market, each with its own frontend, grown over the years as the company grew. Our backend engineers built them alongside everything else, plus an internal admin tool that grew the same way. They all work: thousands of employers run payroll through them every month. But nobody was ever tasked with owning the frontend development, so each one got built the way frontend is built by Backend Developers, seen as a hassle rather than the main aspect users interactive with. What comes next is one frontend that replaces all of them, built from scratch: one quinn app for employers, employees and our own support team, in the browser first, then in the App Store and Google Play from the same work. Alongside it, the frontend of Maestro, the internal tool that replaces the old admin for batch processes. The phone app is the surface that matters most, so everything is built for it from the first screen rather than adapted to it afterwards. That is the opening. How we work We are AI-native, and we mean it operationally rather than as a slogan. AI is how the work gets done here. It is why a small team ships like a large one, and it is a large part of how one person will be able to hold the standard we are describing. We expect you to be at the front of that. Not to have heard of the tools, to live in them, and to build your own leverage with them: scaffolding, visual regression checks, design-token pipelines, whatever takes manual work out of the way. And we expect the judgement that has to come with it. AI writes code that looks right and is subtly wrong: structure that doesn't scale, patterns that fall apart three screens later, components that work once and never again. You take the speed and throw away the rest. AI never lowers the bar here. It is the reason the bar can be this high. Tasks What you will own Everything on the screen: The frontend of the quinn app and the web app. App first. One app for everyone who uses quinn: the employer, the employee, and our own support team working inside the customer's account. The frontend of Maestro, our internal batch tool. Desktop and dense: queues, runs, tables, filters, multi-select, keyboard shortcuts. A different discipline from the app, built on the same components. The component library across quinn Home and quinn Business: one frontend, one experience, every market and every device. Whether the app feels native: response, scrolling, gestures, transitions, biometric login, push. Nothing that gives away it isn't native. The quality of what you ship. Nothing leaves your hands half-finished. Where design ends, engineering begins. We have a design team, and they own how quinn looks and behaves: the flows, the visual design, the tokens, the component specs. You don't design. You own everything from there: how it is built, and everything a design file cannot reasonably specify, such as gestures, keyboard, safe areas, what happens between the drawn breakpoints, the loading, offline, pending and failed states, what a three-line German label does to a layout that was designed for English. You are in the room before design starts, saying what already exists in the library and what a new pattern costs. Not at the end, receiving a handover. When you and design disagree, they decide how it looks and behaves and you decide how it is built. Nothing enters the component library without both of you. Requirements Who we are looking for You care about interfaces more than anyone else in the room. You see the two-pixel misalignment without being told, and it bothers you until it is fixed. You build and maintain UI components and design systems, not one-off screens. You can build a mobile app that feels like one. And you can also build a desktop tool full of tables, filters and keyboard shortcuts, because Maestro is one. You understand UX and how people actually behave, not only how a screen looks. And you write code other people can take over: scalable, structured, documented. Not something that only works while you are in the building. You are independent and decisive. Nobody will spec every detail for you and nobody will review your pixels. You are fluent in English, no other language is required. And if you have a portfolio, a live product, or anything you have shipped that you are proud of, show it to us. Not a requirement, but it tells us more than a CV does. Most importantly: you want this one. Not a frontend role at a company where the frontend is a chore. This one, the app nobody has built yet, the standard nobody has set yet, and a company where getting it right actually decides whether the strategy works. The Team We are a small, fast, direct team. We do not have a lot of process or a lot of hierarchy. We do have a clear strategy, an ambitious plan, and five values we actually mean: Be open, Own it, Speak up, Keep it simple, Bias for action. This is one of the most important hires we will make this year. We are not rushing it and we are not filling a seat. We are looking for the person who reads this and thinks: finally. title: Product manager - gestion des projets (CDI)
description: 🧱 À propos de Bricks Chez Bricks, on construit la façon la plus simple d’investir dans l’immobilier, à partir de 10 €. 670 000+ membres, un produit régulé (PSFP) et une même exigence sur toute l’expérience : permettre d’investir simplement mais aussi de suivre son investissement dans la durée. Bricks est une plateforme à deux faces : d’un côté les investisseurs , de l’autre les porteurs de projets immobiliers . Deux communautés à accompagner et faire grandir en parallèle. Ce qui se passe après le financement d’un projet compte donc autant que le moment où l’on investit : qualité de l’information, transparence, suivi des projets et gestion des situations plus complexes participent directement à l’expérience des deux côtés de la plateforme. Quelques jalons d’une aventure assez unique : passage chez Capital (M6) en 2022, Tony Parker investisseur et ambassadeur, record européen de vitesse de levée : 5 M€ en 5 secondes, 20 M€+ en 10 jours auprès de notre communauté. Côté business : 176 M€ collectés en 2025, +90 % en un an et la rentabilité atteinte. Notre prochain enjeu : scaler à grande échelle sans perdre la vélocité qui fait aujourd’hui partie de notre manière de travailler. Chez Bricks, on attend de chacun qu’il comprenne vraiment les problèmes avant de chercher à les résoudre. L’objectif : prendre les bonnes décisions et construire des solutions utiles. Sur ce poste, ton travail aura un impact direct sur la qualité du suivi des projets et sur la confiance des investisseurs comme des porteurs de projets. Vos missions 🧩 Le job Tu rejoins la squad gestion des projets qui est en charge de tout ce qui se passe après le financement d’un projet immobilier. Faire évoluer la gestion de plusieurs centaines de projets pour qu’elle reste fluide et scalable : priorisation, automatisation, workflows, process et outils. Travailler avec l’engineering pour transformer les problèmes identifiés en solutions produit lorsqu’une solution technique est pertinente. Transformer chaque problème rencontré en apprentissage réutilisable : l’objectif n’est pas de traiter le problème du projet n°237, mais de faire en sorte qu’il soit mieux géré pour les centaines de projets suivants. Et progressivement, prendre de plus en plus d’ownership sur la stratégie et la roadmap de la squad . Le périmètre pourra évoluer fortement selon ce que tu démontres sur le terrain. 👥 La squad Tu travailleras au quotidien avec les équipes en charge du suivi opérationnel des projets ainsi qu’avec l'Engineering, le Product, le Growth et Marketing. Selon les sujets, tu seras également amené à collaborer avec le Care, le juridique ou la direction. Tu dois aller chercher l’information directement auprès des personnes concernées, comprendre leur réalité opérationnelle, croiser les différents points de vue et remonter à la vraie problématique derrière une demande. Ce qu’un utilisateur te demande n’est pas toujours la solution dont il a besoin. Une expérience dans un environnement régulé ou à fortes contraintes métier : fintech, legaltech, comptabilité, RH… est un vrai plus. Tu préfères faire beaucoup avec une petite équipe plutôt que de construire du process pour construire du process ❌ Tu ne fitteras probablement pas si Tu as besoin d’un framework très établi pour fonctionner. title: Engineering Manager - Hands-on (CDI)
description: 🏗️ À propos de Bricks Chez Bricks, on construit la façon la plus simple d’investir dans l’immobilier, à partir de 10 €. Aujourd’hui, plus de 670 000 membres utilisent notre plateforme. Quelques jalons : passage chez Capital (M6) en 2022, Tony Parker investisseur et ambassadeur, record européen de vitesse de levée avec 5 M€ collectés en 5 secondes , puis plus de 20 M€ en 10 jours auprès de notre communauté. En 2025, Bricks a collecté 176 M€ , soit +90 % en un an, tout en atteignant la rentabilité. Derrière cette croissance, il y a un produit B2C régulé, des flux financiers réels, des enjeux forts de sécurité, de fiabilité et de cohérence des données. Ce qui part en production peut être utilisé par des milliers d’investisseurs dans les heures qui suivent. Côté Engineering, on fonctionne avec une équipe autonome, proche du produit et du business. On attend de chacun qu’il comprenne les problèmes en profondeur, prenne des décisions et contribue directement à la qualité de ce qu’on construit. Vos missions 🧩 Le job Tu rejoindras une équipe Engineering de 10 ingénieurs , avec un CTO qui code au quotidien. Côté Produit : 2 Designers et 2 PM. L’équipe grandit, les enjeux aussi. On cherche aujourd’hui un Engineering Manager qui travaillera étroitement avec le CTO , à la fois sur le management de l’équipe, son organisation et les sujets techniques structurants. Tu participeras aux roadmaps Engineering, à la composition des squads, à la définition des objectifs et aux prochains recrutements , tout en restant proche du code et du produit. Chez Bricks, devenir manager ne veut pas dire s’éloigner de la technique : tu dois pouvoir entrer dans une discussion d’architecture, challenger une décision, faire une code review utile ou débloquer un sujet complexe. 🧱 Ce que tu vas owner 👉 Construire l’organisation Engineering avec le CTO : faire évoluer la composition des équipes, les objectifs, les façons de travailler et participer activement aux recrutements. 👉 Manager et faire progresser les ingénieurs au quotidien : 1:1, feedback, accompagnement, progression, exigence technique. Comprendre ce qui bloque quelqu’un et l’aider à passer au palier suivant. 👉 Rester connecté au code et au produit. Tu ne coderas pas nécessairement toute la journée, mais tu dois pouvoir entrer dans la codebase, participer aux reviews et prendre part aux décisions d’architecture. 👉 Créer les conditions pour que l’équipe shippe vite et bien. Identifier les blocages, arbitrer, clarifier les responsabilités et faire évoluer le process uniquement lorsqu’il apporte de la valeur. 👉 Maintenir un haut niveau d’exigence technique. Modélisation du domaine, architecture, qualité des données, sécurité, performance : tu aides l’équipe à prendre les bonnes décisions là où elles comptent vraiment. 🛠️ La stack Tu dois être suffisamment proche de notre environnement technique pour pouvoir intervenir réellement dans les discussions et dans le code : 👉 TypeScript end-to-end. Les types sont de la documentation qui s’exécute. 👉 Node monolithe, Screaming Architecture. 👉 Postgres (NeonDB) avec Graphile pour les queues ACID. Redis pour ce qui doit être rapide. 👉 Zod, Kysely, ts-pattern - type-safety du front à la DB. 👉 Better Auth. 👉 Railway pour l’infra. 👉 Github CI, Datadog, K6. 👉 React Native + RN Web côté front : une seul codebase web + mobile. Tu n’as pas besoin d’avoir utilisé exactement chacune de ces technos. En revanche, Node/TypeScript et une vraie profondeur backend sont importants : on cherche quelqu’un capable de challenger techniquement l’équipe, pas seulement de la manager. 🤖 IA-first mindset L’IA est partout dans notre quotidien. 100**% des workflows passe par elle** : Claude Code, Claude Cowork, Cursor, Automations, etc. Et pour un Engineering Manager, l’enjeu va plus loin que sa propre utilisation : tu dois comprendre comment l’IA transforme la façon de manager, coder, de reviewer, de tester, de recruter et de faire progresser une équipe Engineering. Si tu vois encore l’IA comme secondaire, ce poste n’est pas pour toi. Vos compétences 🎯 Tu fitteras si... 👉 Tu as d’abord été Senior Software Engineer et tu n’as pas quitté la technique en devenant manager. Tu aimes toujours le code, tu restes proche des sujets techniques et tu peux encore mettre les mains dedans quand c’est nécessaire. 👉 Tu sais construire et faire vivre une équipe Engineering. Recruter, intégrer, faire progresser, donner du feedback et faire évoluer les responsabilités font partie du rôle. 👉 Tu as une forte expérience backend Node /TypeScript en environnement produit. 👉 Tu sais prendre de la hauteur. Au-delà du management individuel, tu réfléchis à la composition des équipes, aux responsabilités, aux recrutements et à la façon dont l’organisation doit évoluer. 👉 Tu sais quand ralentir et quand shipper. Tout ne mérite pas 3 semaines de réflexion, mais tout ne mérite pas non plus un quick fix. 👉 Tu es pragmatique et tu préfères construire une organisation adaptée au contexte plutôt qu’appliquer un playbook tout fait. 👉 Tu reconnais tes erreurs sans en faire un drame. Tu peux changer d’avis quand quelqu’un apporte de meilleurs arguments. 👉 La fintech, l’investissement ou l’immobilier t’intéresse : gros bonus si tu investis toi-même. ❌ Tu ne fitteras pas si... 👉 Tu veux sortir de la technique en devenant manager. 👉 Tu cherches un rôle principalement centré sur le delivery, les cérémonies et le suivi de process. 👉 Tu veux appliquer un modèle d’organisation tout fait, sans l’adapter au contexte. 👉 Tu as besoin d’une séparation nette entre management, technique et produit. 👉 Tu veux être le point de passage de toutes les décisions techniques. Ici, ton rôle est aussi de faire grandir des ingénieurs autonomes , pas de décider à leur place. Avantages L'offre 👉 CDI, temps plein. 👉 Un produit B2C utilisé par 700 000+ membres, ce que ton équipe construit a un impact concret et immédiat. 👉 Un rôle au cœur de l’organisation Engineering : tu travailleras directement avec le CTO et auras un impact réel sur la façon dont l’équipe se structure et évolue. 👉 Une boîte ambitieuse, rentable et en forte croissance 👉 Salaire compétitif, MacBook Pro de ton choix, tout le matériel qu’il te faut. 👉 Hybride Montpellier : office-first (2j/sem de remote) ou remote-first (~2j/mois au bureau). Déroulement des entretiens Pré-qualification téléphonique avec notre recruteuse Echange manager avec Denis, notre CTO (1h) Entretien technique : cadrage technique et implémentation d'une fonctionnalité Entretien team-fit (1h) Rencontre avec Cédric, notre fondateur (45 min) Offre Find more English Speaking Jobs in France on Arbeitnow

title: Edge & Machine Integration Engineer (PLC to Cloud), Freelance, m/f/d
description: FALU AG in Rüti (ZH) builds and sells swab production machines that run in plants around the world. With FALU PMAS, our cloud based production monitoring and assistance system, every machine reports its state every five seconds. Customers get live dashboards, shift KPIs, downtime analytics and automatic alerts in the browser. The first customer went live in September 2026 with eight machines, and more plants are lined up. The cloud side of PMAS is built and running in production: broker, ingestion service, databases, web app. The path from the PLC inside the machine to the MQTT broker is covered by one engineer who designed and built it. With more machines and more plants coming, that one person is no longer enough. We are looking for a freelancer who adds capacity on exactly this path: PLC software, Raspberry Pi edge devices, site gateway, broker connection. This is a permanent role that we staff on a freelance basis: no project end date, a long term engagement with about 1 week of work per month, with more when a rollout is on. You will work directly with our existing integration engineer, our inhouse engineering team and the CEO. Tasks You work on everything between the machine PLC and the MQTT broker, alongside the engineer who built the current setup. Which parts you take over completely and which you share depends on your strengths. Concretely: PLC and machine side Bring the PMAS message format into the CB1 machine software (Siemens S7, TIA Portal V18 with HMI) and keep it in sync with the payload contract: cumulative counters, machine status, error codes, timestamps from the PLC clock. Decide and implement how data leaves the PLC: MQTT publishing from the PLC itself, or a read on the edge device (S7 protocol or OPC UA) that publishes on its behalf. Pick one, justify it, standardise it. Manage PLC software versions across the fleet, including safe update and rollback procedures for machines already running at customers. Ensure clock discipline on the PLCs (NTP, local time zone per plant), since every duration KPI is computed from PLC timestamps. Edge devices and site gateway Develop and maintain the software on the Raspberry Pi based edge devices next to each machine: MQTT client, buffering and store and forward during uplink outages, unique client IDs, credential handling, health reporting. Develop and maintain the site gateway: isolated machine network, routing and firewall, outbound only TLS and NTP, remote maintenance access, watchdogs, recovery from a spare device. Help turn the current setup into a provisioning process: golden image, per machine configuration, fleet wide updates without a site visit. A new machine goes from unboxing to "visible in the dashboard" in under an hour. Monitor the edge layer so that we know about a degraded device before the customer does. Broker and data contract Administer the HiveMQ Cloud clusters per customer: credentials, topic ACLs, client ID scheme, certificates. Maintain the payload contract together with the existing integration engineer. Changes are versioned and documented. Commissioning and support Onboard new customers and new machines end to end, remotely where possible and on site where needed (primarily Europe and the United States). Act as second line when "the dashboard shows nothing" or "the numbers look wrong" and the cause sits between PLC and broker. Write the documentation you would have wanted on day one: onboarding sheets, runbooks, wiring notes. Requirements Must have Siemens PLC programming in TIA Portal (SCL and LAD, S7-1200/1500 family). You can open an existing machine project, understand it and change it without breaking the machine. Industrial networking: PROFINET, VLANs, static and DHCP setups, firewalls, TLS basics. You have connected a machine to a network that was not built for it. Linux on Raspberry Pi or comparable single board computers: systemd, networking, images, headless operation, remote administration. Solid programming skills in Python or Node.js for edge software, and Git as a daily tool. MQTT in depth: versions 3.1.1 and 5.0, QoS levels, retained messages, last will, TLS, broker ACLs. Proficiency with AI coding tools is a hard requirement. You use Claude Code, Cursor, Copilot or comparable tools every day, you write and maintain project instructions for them, you review their output critically, and you are measurably faster with them than without. Our code and documentation are written with and for these tools. If you see AI tools as optional, this role is not for you. Working proficiency in English (all code, commits and documentation are in English). German is a plus for the machine side. Willingness to travel to customer plants, typically a few days per quarter. Availability of at least two days per week on a permanent basis, with the option to scale up during rollouts. You work as a freelancer (own company or registered self employed) and can invoice FALU AG. Nice to have OPC UA, Snap7 or the Siemens open communication libraries. Node-RED, Docker on ARM, Ansible or similar fleet tooling. Machine building or commissioning experience: reading electrical schematics, 24 V control cabinet basics, HMI (WinCC). Administration of HiveMQ, Mosquitto or EMQX. A basic understanding of what happens after the broker (Node.js services, PostgreSQL, ClickHouse), so that you can talk to the cloud side at eye level. Benefits A clearly bounded, business critical scope with a colleague who knows the system and hands over properly. No cold start. A running production system with a real customer, not a greenfield slide deck. AI assisted development is how we work, not an experiment. You get the tools and the budget for them. Machines you can touch: a test bench at FALU in Rüti with real PLCs and edge hardware. Remote by default, on site in Rüti when hardware is involved. Travel to customer plants is paid on top of the rate. A permanent role, not a project with an end date: growing volume as more plants go live, on a freelance basis for as long as it works for both sides. Fast, uncomplicated invoicing and decisions from a small team. If you have ever made a stubborn PLC talk to the cloud and have capacity to do it again with us, we would like to hear from you. Please send us your CV or LinkedIn profile, your daily rate and availability, one paragraph about a PLC to cloud integration you built or fixed and what went wrong on the way, and one concrete example of how you use AI tools in your daily engineering work. What to expect: a short call with Marc Wyss (CEO) within a week of your application, then a small practical task with a simulated PLC data source, a Raspberry Pi image and a broker endpoint. We look at how you work, not just at the result. After that, one conversation with our integration engineer and the team, then a decision and a contract. title: Cloud Operations Lead
description: Welcome to Xelon – where technology meets innovation and customer centricity. As we continue to grow our Platform team, we are looking for a Cloud Operations Lead (80-100%) to join our team. In this role, you own the daily operation of our cloud platform: availability, incidents, recovery, and the service desk that customers reach first. When something has to keep running at Xelon, you make it run. At Xelon , we deliver secure, scalable, and automated Swiss cloud infrastructure for the next generation of digital services. From IaaS to SaaS , our platform powers workloads in regulated industries like technology , finance, insurance, and public services . Our solutions - Xelon Cloud , Xelon Secure+ and Xelon HQ combine reliability, automation, sovereignty, and simplicity in one ecosystem. We are on a mission to become the #1 Swiss Cloud Enabler , and we are growing a team of people who want to shape the future of cloud infrastructure and software operations. Tasks Your Mission As Cloud Operations Lead you own the daily operation of our cloud platform: availability, incident response, monitoring, backup and recovery, and the infrastructure underneath. The service desk is part of your team, so you also own what customers experience every time they contact us. You lead a team of four to six people, and you are the person the business relies on when something has to keep running. Xelon is building a new platform over the coming years. VMware carries the production estate through that transition and stays in place for at least the next two years, alongside other hypervisors. You run that environment, you keep it stable and auditable, and you make sure the transition never happens at the expense of the customers on it. Platform strategy, target architecture and the technology roadmap sit with the Head of Platform & Technology. You are a close partner in those decisions and you own their operational reality. What You Own in the First 12 Months Availability and customer satisfaction. You hit the agreed availability targets and hold them, and customers experience both the platform and the service desk as dependable, with incidents resolved quickly and communicated clearly. ISO 27001 and audit readiness. Operational evidence, documentation and patch compliance stay audit-ready throughout the year instead of being assembled in the weeks before each audit. Team depth. No critical part of the platform depends on one person, and every engineer in the team has a development path they can name. Responsibilities Operations and multi-hypervisor environment: Operate and optimise the production estate across a multi-hypervisor environment, with VMware as the primary platform. Keep availability, performance and capacity ahead of demand as the customer base grows. Own hardware lifecycle, capacity planning and datacenter operations together with our partners. Networking, storage and datacenter: Own the operational side of network and storage: segmentation, routing, firewalling, DNS, load balancing, and the storage layer underneath the platform. Raise the level of networking knowledge and practice across the team. Monitoring, incident response and recovery: Run and improve monitoring, alerting and logging so that problems surface before customers report them. Own backup and disaster recovery, including proving that restores actually work. Service desk and customer support: Lead the service desk: intake, triage, ticket quality and response times against agreed service levels. Own what customers experience when they contact us, from the first response through to clear communication during an incident. Act as escalation point for 1st and 2nd level support incidents. Turn recurring tickets into fixes together with the engineering side of the team, rather than absorbing them as routine. Team leadership: Lead, coach and develop a team of four to six people across cloud operations and the service desk. Build development plans and remove single points of knowledge. Set on-call, shift and service desk coverage the team can sustain. Automation and process: Move recurring manual operations into Infrastructure as Code and scripting. Improve the operational toolchain and the handover points with DevOps, Support and Product. Apply service management practice where it reduces friction, not as an end in itself. Compliance and audit readiness: Keep operations aligned with ISO 27001, ISAE and Swiss data sovereignty requirements. Work with Dev- and SecOps on hardening, patch compliance and audit evidence. Maintain operational documentation that holds up in an audit. Budget, vendors and procurement: Co-own the operational CAPEX and OPEX budget with the Head of Platform & Technology. Manage vendor relationships, licenses and procurement for the operations estate. Requirements Who You Are We are looking for an operations leader, not an architect. Technical depth matters, and so does the ability to run a team through a platform transition without dropping the service underneath it. You keep the service running while the ground moves. A platform transition does not become the customer's problem. You lead through presence and clarity, not authority. Your team knows what good looks like. You are calm in an incident and precise afterwards. The postmortem produces a fix, not a narrative. You treat the service desk as part of the product, not as a queue to be absorbed. You tell your manager what is broken and what you need to fix it. Must Haves Leadership: 5+ years leading IT operations, in a cloud, hosting or service provider environment. VMware: hands-on experience in production. You have operated it yourself, not only overseen it. Infrastructure: practical working knowledge of networking, storage and datacenter operations. German and English: you communicate confidently in both, spoken and written. Work authorisation: Swiss or EU/EFTA citizenship, or a valid Swiss work permit. Nice to Haves Networking at provider scale — a strong plus: segmentation, routing, firewalling, load balancing and DNS. Experience with other hypervisors alongside VMware, and with hypervisor migrations. Hands-on Infrastructure as Code, e.g. Terraform or Ansible. Monitoring and logging at scale, e.g. Prometheus, Grafana or a similar stack. Operating experience in a regulated environment: ISO 27001, ISAE or SOC 2. Running operations through a platform migration or a consolidation. Benefits What Xelon Offers A leadership role with real ownership in a Swiss cloud provider, not a coordination layer. A platform in transition, which means your operational decisions change something visible. Office in Zug with a hybrid working model, 80 to 100 percent. Direct collaboration with the Head of Platform & Technology and cross-functional teams. A team small enough that you know what everyone is working on. Competitive salary, modern tooling and a product-driven environment with clarity and ownership. Join Our Mission Do you feel like you are the person that would complete our team? Are you ready for a new challenge? Then apply now. We look forward to hearing from you. The Xelon Team Find more English Speaking Jobs in Switzerland on Arbeitnow

title: Chief Operating Officer (COO)
description: VAULTED AG is a Swiss deep-tech scale-up born out of research at ETH Zurich and the EMPA innovation ecosystem. Our core technology is the Rippmann Floor System® (RFS), a lightweight, prefabricated structural floor system that reduces concrete use by up to 70%, steel use by up to 90%, and embodied carbon by up to 75% compared with conventional concrete slabs. Location: Dübendorf ZH, Switzerland · Start date: Q1 2027 · 100% · Reporting to the CEO Tasks We are hiring a Chief Operating Officer to build the operational engine that turns confirmed projects into reliable, profitable, and scalable delivery. This is a senior leadership role for someone who combines deep project and construction industry understanding with strong operational and commercial judgement, but also someone who is very hands-on and enjoys setting up the systems and processes behind our operations. The COO takes ownership once a project is won and oversees project delivery, project management, supplier and prefabrication partnerships, operational contracting, and project economics. The role ensures that scope, timelines, quality, risks, resources, costs, and margins are transparent and actively managed, while giving project teams the structure and support they need to deliver. A core mandate is to make VAULTED better with every project: translate project learnings into stronger processes, supplier setups, handovers, delivery standards, and feedback to engineering and R&D. Contracting, procurement & operational risk: Shape supplier and operational contracts, procurement approaches, and partnership models that improve delivery certainty, manage risk, protect margins, and maintain strategic flexibility. Cross-functional leadership & resources: Connect project management, engineering, design, R&D, commercial teams, and external partners. Create clarity on priorities, responsibilities, capacity, and trade-offs, and ensure smooth handovers from sales into execution. Continuous improvement & international scaling: Turn project learnings into better processes, standards, supplier setups, and execution methods, while building operational readiness for Switzerland, Belgium, the UK, the US, and future markets. Proven responsibility for complex, multi-stakeholder projects or project portfolios, with the ability to oversee execution while staying close enough to intervene when needed. Strong practical understanding of how construction or engineered products move from design and procurement through production, coordination, and delivery. Strong commercial and financial discipline, including project budgets, cost drivers, forecasting, margins, change management, and operational risk. Experience negotiating and managing suppliers, production partners, contracts, and long-term operational relationships. Strong leadership skills with high empathy and high standards: able to build trust, set clear expectations, challenge constructively, make decisions, and hold teams and partners to commitments. Strategic and hands-on working style: able to build scalable systems and processes while staying pragmatic, close to project realities, and comfortable solving difficult execution issues. Fluency in English is required; German is a strong advantage. Based in Zurich/Dübendorf, or willing to work primarily from Dübendorf, with occasional national and international travel to project, production, and construction sites.
